facts.one_liner: A three-tiered Roman aqueduct bridge over the Gardon River.
facts.why_go: Built in the 1st century AD, the Pont du Gard is the highest Roman aqueduct bridge, standing about 48 metres tall. It carried water to the Roman city of Nemausus (Nîmes). It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and visitors can swim in the river below in summer.
facts.best_time: May–September; the river is good for swimming in summer.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 25 km from Nîmes and Avignon; buses run from both.
facts.good_to_know: There is a museum and visitor centre on site. Parking fees apply.

facts.one_liner: A fairy-tale medieval walled city with 52 towers.
facts.why_go: La Cité de Carcassonne is a hilltop fortress with two rings of walls and 52 towers. It was restored in the 19th century by Eugène Viollet-le-Duc, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Old Bridge over the Aude links it to the lower town.
facts.best_time: Spring and autumn; Bastille Day fireworks on 14 July.
facts.how_to_get_there: Carcassonne station is on the Toulouse–Narbonne line; the Cité is a 30-minute walk or bus ride.
facts.good_to_know: Visit the Château Comtal and ramparts with a ticket. Evening walks are quiet once day-trippers leave.

image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Abadía de Westminster, Londres, Inglaterra, 2022-11-23, DD 67-69 HDR.jpg' (6870×4580) confirms Westminster Abbey; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: Westminster Abbey, London, England

facts.one_liner: London’s Gothic coronation church and burial place of monarchs.
facts.why_go: Westminster Abbey has been the coronation church of English and British monarchs since 1066. The current Gothic building dates largely from the 13th century. Kings, queens, poets and scientists such as Isaac Newton and Charles Darwin are buried here. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with the Palace of Westminster.
facts.best_time: Year-round; weekday mornings are quieter.
facts.how_to_get_there: Westminster or St James’s Park Underground stations.
facts.good_to_know: The Abbey is closed to sightseers on Sundays, when you can attend services.

image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Edinburgh Castle Rock.jpg' (4256×2832) confirms Edinburgh Castle; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: Edinburgh Castle is situated on top of an ancient volcano that allows it to dominate the city skyline even today. Edinburgh Scotland, UK

facts.one_liner: A fortress on an extinct volcano above Scotland’s capital.
facts.why_go: Edinburgh Castle sits on Castle Rock, an extinct volcanic plug, dominating the skyline. It houses the Honours of Scotland (the Scottish crown jewels), the Stone of Destiny and St Margaret’s Chapel, Edinburgh’s oldest building. The One O’Clock Gun is fired every day except Sundays.
facts.best_time: Year-round; August brings the Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo.
facts.how_to_get_there: At the top of the Royal Mile, about 15 minutes’ walk from Edinburgh Waverley station.
facts.good_to_know: Book tickets online. Allow at least 2 hours.

facts.one_liner: A 1,000-year-old fortress guarding the Crown Jewels.
facts.why_go: Founded by William the Conqueror in the 1070s, the Tower of London has been a royal palace, prison and treasury. The White Tower is its oldest part, and the Crown Jewels are displayed here. Yeoman Warders lead tours, and ravens are kept on site. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.best_time: Year-round; arrive at opening to see the Crown Jewels first.
facts.how_to_get_there: Tower Hill Underground station; Tower Gateway on the DLR.
facts.good_to_know: Book tickets online. Yeoman Warder tours are included.

facts.one_liner: Twin Gothic spires rising above the Rhine.
facts.why_go: Construction began in 1248 and finished in 1880, making Cologne Cathedral the largest Gothic church in Northern Europe. Its twin spires rise 157 metres. The cathedral holds the Shrine of the Three Kings and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. You can climb 533 steps to a viewing platform.
facts.best_time: Year-round; December for the Christmas markets.
facts.how_to_get_there: Right next to Köln Hauptbahnhof (main station).
facts.good_to_know: Entry to the cathedral is free; the tower and treasury charge.

facts.one_liner: One of the world’s largest castle complexes, above the Vltava.
facts.why_go: Prague Castle was founded in the 9th century and is one of the largest ancient castle complexes in the world. It includes St Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, St George’s Basilica and Golden Lane. It is the seat of the Czech president.
facts.best_time: Spring and autumn; early morning before tour groups.
facts.how_to_get_there: Tram 22 to Pražský hrad, or walk up from Malá Strana.
facts.good_to_know: The castle grounds are free; the main buildings need a ticket.

facts.one_liner: The Habsburgs’ baroque summer palace with vast formal gardens.
facts.why_go: Schönbrunn was the summer residence of the Habsburg emperors. The palace has 1,441 rooms, and its gardens include the Gloriette, a hilltop colonnade with views over Vienna, and the world’s oldest zoo. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.best_time: April–October for the gardens.
facts.how_to_get_there: U4 subway to Schönbrunn or Hietzing.
facts.good_to_know: The gardens are free. Book palace tours online in summer.

facts.one_liner: A Manueline fortress on the Tagus from the Age of Discovery.
facts.why_go: Built in the early 16th century, Belém Tower guarded the entrance to Lisbon’s harbour and marked the departure point of explorers. Its Manueline decoration includes ropes, armillary spheres and a rhinoceros carving. With the nearby Jerónimos Monastery it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.best_time: Spring and autumn; sunset over the river is lovely.
facts.how_to_get_there: Tram 15E from central Lisbon to Belém.
facts.good_to_know: Interior spaces are small and queues can be long. The tower is closed on Mondays.

image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Centro Histórico, 16.9 -- 2023 -- Córdoba, España.jpg' (5984×3366) confirms Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: Views of the Historic centre of Córdoba from the Guadalquivir River, from where the Mosque-Cathedral and the Roman Bridge stand out, declared a World Heritage S

facts.one_liner: A forest of red-and-white arches where a cathedral rises inside a great mosque.
facts.why_go: The Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba was begun in 785 as a mosque under the Umayyads and later became a cathedral. Its prayer hall has hundreds of columns with red-and-white striped arches, and a Renaissance cathedral nave was built in its centre in the 16th century. It is part of the Historic Centre of Córdoba UNESCO site.
facts.best_time: March–May and October–November; summer is extremely hot.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 15 minutes’ walk from the Roman Bridge; high-speed trains reach Córdoba from Madrid and Seville.
facts.good_to_know: Morning visits are often free at certain times—check the official site. Night tours run in season.

facts.one_liner: A Roman aqueduct of granite blocks held without mortar.
facts.why_go: The Roman aqueduct of Segovia was built around the 1st–2nd century AD. Over 160 arches stretch across the city, built from granite blocks without mortar, with the highest section about 28 metres. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with the Old Town of Segovia.
facts.best_time: Spring and autumn.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 30 minutes by high-speed train from Madrid.
facts.good_to_know: Climb the steps next to the aqueduct for views. Try roast suckling pig, a local speciality.

image.attribution: Photo: Bernard Gagnon, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Roussanou Monastery, Meteora.jpg' (3316×2211) confirms Meteora; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: Roussanou Monastery, Meteora, Greece

facts.one_liner: Monasteries perched on towering sandstone pillars.
facts.why_go: At Meteora, Eastern Orthodox monks began building monasteries on top of soaring sandstone pillars in the 14th century, seeking isolation from the world. Of the 24 that once existed, six are still active, including the Great Meteoron and Varlaam. For centuries supplies and visitors were hauled up in nets and on rope ladders; today rock-cut steps lead to the doors. The rocks glow at sunset, and the site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.best_time: April–June and September–October for mild weather and clear light.
facts.how_to_get_there: Kalambaka and Kastraki are the gateway villages; direct trains from Athens to Kalambaka take about 4–5 hours.
facts.good_to_know: Each monastery closes on a different weekday—check before you go. Women must wear skirts (wraps are lent at the doors) and shoulders must be covered.

facts.one_liner: The sanctuary of Apollo and the ancient oracle on Mount Parnassus.
facts.why_go: Delphi was the most important sanctuary in ancient Greece, home to the Oracle of Apollo. The ruins include the Temple of Apollo, the theatre, stadium and the Tholos at the Sanctuary of Athena Pronaia. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.best_time: April–June and September–October.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 2.5 hours by road from Athens.
facts.good_to_know: Wear good shoes for the steep path. Visit the museum to see the Charioteer of Delphi.

image.author: Diego Delso
image.attribution: Photo: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Templo de Karnak, Luxor, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 142.jpg' (8016×4295) confirms Karnak Temple; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: Karnak Temple, Luxor, Egypt

facts.one_liner: A vast temple complex with a forest of giant columns.
facts.why_go: Karnak is one of the largest religious complexes ever built, expanded by pharaohs over some 2,000 years and dedicated mainly to the god Amun-Ra. Its Great Hypostyle Hall is a forest of 134 colossal sandstone columns covered in carvings, and obelisks, sacred lake and avenues of ram-headed sphinxes complete the scene. It is part of the Ancient Thebes UNESCO World Heritage Site, linked to Luxor Temple by the restored Avenue of Sphinxes.
facts.best_time: October–April for cooler weather; arrive at opening time in any season.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 3 km north of central Luxor by taxi or horse-drawn carriage; Luxor has an international airport and overnight trains from Cairo.
facts.good_to_know: There is little shade—bring water, a hat and sunscreen. An evening sound-and-light show runs most nights.

facts.one_liner: A Greek-temple memorial overlooking the Reflecting Pool.
facts.why_go: Dedicated in 1922, the Lincoln Memorial honours President Abraham Lincoln with a 19-foot seated statue. Its 36 Doric columns represent the states of the Union at Lincoln’s death. Martin Luther King Jr delivered his ‘I Have a Dream’ speech on its steps in 1963.
facts.best_time: Spring for cherry blossoms; evenings for a calm, lit-up view.
facts.how_to_get_there: Foggy Bottom Metro station is about 15 minutes’ walk away.
facts.good_to_know: Open 24 hours with no admission charge.

image.attribution: Photo: Daniel Schwen, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:St Louis night expblend.jpg' (3000×1929) confirms Gateway Arch; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: St. Louis on the Mississippi river by night. Jefferson National Expansion Memorial aka. Gateway Arch and Old Courthouse are visible.

facts.one_liner: A 630-foot stainless-steel arch on the Mississippi.
facts.why_go: Completed in 1965 to a design by architect Eero Saarinen, the stainless-steel Gateway Arch rises 630 feet over the Mississippi riverfront and is the tallest human-made monument in the Western Hemisphere. It commemorates the westward expansion of the United States. Small tram pods carry visitors to an observation deck at the top, and the museum beneath the arch tells the story of the American West.
facts.best_time: April–June and September–October; sunset turns the steel gold.
facts.how_to_get_there: In downtown St. Louis; the 8th & Pine and Convention Center MetroLink stations are a short walk away, and St. Louis Lambert Airport (STL) is about 25 minutes by car or train.
facts.good_to_know: Book tram tickets in advance—the pods are small and not ideal for claustrophobic visitors. Riverboat cruises leave from the levee below.

The tower was illuminated in green in honor o

facts.one_liner: The Art Deco tower that defined the Manhattan skyline.
facts.why_go: Completed in 1931 in just over a year, the Empire State Building was the tallest building in the world for nearly 40 years and remains a symbol of New York. Its Art Deco lobby is a landmark in its own right, and the open-air 86th-floor deck and the 102nd-floor observatory give sweeping views over Manhattan, the rivers and beyond. The tower’s top is lit in changing colours for holidays and events.
facts.best_time: Year-round; clear days, sunset and late evening for city lights.
facts.how_to_get_there: At Fifth Avenue and 34th Street; 34th Street–Herald Square subway station is a block away.
facts.good_to_know: Book timed tickets online. The 86th-floor deck is open late, and late-night visits are usually quieter.

image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Hoover Dam and Black Canyon seen from the Mike O'Callaghan–Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge, panorama, Arizona–Nevada.jpg' (11000×9243) confirms Hoover Dam; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: Overhead view of the downstream face of Hoover Dam in Black Canyon on the Colorado River, with the two powerhouse wings, the four intake towers on the crest, an

facts.one_liner: A massive concrete dam in Black Canyon on the Colorado River.
facts.why_go: Built during the Great Depression and completed in 1936, Hoover Dam rises about 726 feet in Black Canyon on the Colorado River, on the border between Nevada and Arizona. It created Lake Mead, one of the largest reservoirs in the United States, and its Art Deco design and scale make it an engineering landmark. The Mike O’Callaghan–Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge gives a dramatic view down onto the dam.
facts.best_time: October–April; summer temperatures in the canyon are extremely hot.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 45 minutes’ drive south-east of Las Vegas via Boulder City.
facts.good_to_know: Guided tours inside the dam have limited capacity; vehicles pass a security checkpoint. Parking at the visitor centre is paid.

image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Sacsayhuamán, Cusco, Perú, 2015-07-31, DD 40.JPG' (8623×4675) confirms Sacsayhuamán; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: Sacsayhuamán, Cusco, Peru

facts.one_liner: Massive Inca stone walls fitted without mortar.
facts.why_go: Sacsayhuamán is an Inca fortress-temple on a hill above Cusco, built mainly in the 15th century. Its three tiers of zigzag walls are made of enormous limestone blocks—some weighing well over 100 tonnes—cut to fit together so precisely that no mortar was needed. Every 24 June it hosts the re-enacted Inti Raymi, the Inca Festival of the Sun. It is part of the City of Cuzco UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.best_time: May–September, the dry season; late June for Inti Raymi.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 2 km uphill from Cusco’s Plaza de Armas—walk via San Cristóbal church or take a taxi.
facts.good_to_know: Entry is included in the Boleto Turístico del Cusco. At 3,700 metres, take the climb slowly.

image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Sydney harbour bridge new south wales.jpg' (2599×1494) confirms Sydney Harbour Bridge; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: Sydney Harbour Bridge

facts.one_liner: The ‘Coathanger’ steel arch over Sydney Harbour.
facts.why_go: Opened in 1932, the Sydney Harbour Bridge—nicknamed ‘the Coathanger’—is one of the world’s largest steel arch bridges, linking the city centre with the North Shore. Pedestrians can walk across its eastern footway for views of the Opera House, climb to the top of the arch with BridgeClimb, or visit the Pylon Lookout museum. It is the centrepiece of Sydney’s famous New Year’s Eve fireworks.
facts.best_time: Year-round; sunset and New Year’s Eve are special.
facts.how_to_get_there: Walk up from The Rocks via the Argyle Stairs, or take the train to Milsons Point on the north side.
facts.good_to_know: BridgeClimb must be booked and includes a breath test. Ferries from Circular Quay give the best views from the water.
